subject.title: Bug: Orphaned TaskFlows in `waiting` status permanently block agent heartbeats (requests-in-flight deadlock)

question: What default abandonment contract should OpenClaw apply to durable managed TaskFlows in `waiting` state when their external callback never arrives?
rationale: The current API intentionally allows durable waits without a deadline, so automation cannot safely choose between preserving long waits and force-ending orphaned waits without maintainer product/API intent.

options.title: Owner-declared deadlines
options.body: Add controller-visible deadline or orphan metadata and expire only waits whose owner opted into or proves abandonment.

options.title: Manual repair only
options.body: Keep stale waits as diagnostics and provide a documented operator repair path without changing the default runtime lifecycle.

options.title: Global default timeout
options.body: Apply a uniform timeout to all waiting flows, accepting the compatibility risk for plugins with legitimate long waits.

recommendation.title: Owner-declared deadlines
recommendation.body: Add controller-visible deadline or orphan metadata and expire only waits whose owner opted into or proves abandonment.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest recent history across TaskFlow maintenance, audit, and runtime type boundaries where the contract would be defined.
